journey.title: Focus stays in the results dialog after Show all removes itself
journey.goal: Activating a control that removes itself keeps keyboard focus inside the trapped dialog

functionalJourney.title: Show all results with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: The dialog opens, lists every result and closes

guards.title: Escape closes results and returns focus
guards.goal: Escape dismisses the dialog and focus returns to the trigger

plan.root_cause: When the 'Show all 4 results' button is removed from the DOM after being focused, the focus-trap attempts to restore focus to the removed button (which is no longer in the document) when focus escapes the trap. This results in focus being lost to the body instead of remaining inside the dialog.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the checkFocusIn function to verify that the most recently focused node is still in the document before attempting to restore focus to it. If it is not, fall back to the initial focus node (which is known to be in the trap).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will remain trapped inside the dialog after the 'Show all 4 results' button is removed, ensuring that keyboard users can continue to interact with the dialog without losing focus.
functional_risks: The change adds a document.contains check which may have a minimal performance impact, but it is only executed when focus escapes the trap (a rare event).

If the most recently focused node is still in the document but no longer in the trap's containers (due to container changes or node movement), the trap may incorrectly attempt to restore focus to that node instead of the initial focus node. However, this scenario is unlikely and the trap would still keep focus within the document (though possibly outside the intended trap area).
verification_requirements: Verify that after clicking the 'Show all 4 results' button, focus remains inside the dialog (e.g., pressing Tab moves focus to the close button or the first item in the list).
Ensure that the existing functionality of the focus-trap is preserved for other cases (e.g., pressing Escape still closes the dialog and restores focus to the opener).

plan.root_cause: When the 'Show all 4 results' button is activated, it removes itself from the DOM. The focus trap's `checkFocusIn` handler attempts to restore focus to the most recently focused node (the removed button) when focus escapes to the body. Since the button is no longer in the document, focusing it fails, and focus remains on the body instead of being trapped inside the dialog.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify `checkFocusIn` to update the tabbable nodes (so the removed button is no longer considered) and then verify that the most recently focused node is still within the trap's containers before attempting to restore focus to it. If not, fall back to the initial focus node (which will be the close button after the update).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: After activating the 'Show all 4 results' button, keyboard focus will remain inside the dialog, allowing the user to continue navigating the results with Tab/Shift+Tab.
functional_risks: Updating tabbable nodes on every focus escape could have a minor performance impact, but focus escape is rare.
The change might affect other escape scenarios, but the logic is more robust.
verification_requirements: Verify that after clicking 'Show all 4 results', pressing Tab moves focus to the close button (or first focusable element in the dialog).
Ensure that pressing Escape still closes the dialog and returns focus to the opener.
Test that the focus trap works correctly when focus escapes via other means (e.g., clicking outside).

plan.root_cause: When the 'Show all 4 results' button (#more) is activated, it removes itself from the DOM. The focus trap's `checkFocusIn` handler still holds a reference to this removed button as `state.mostRecentlyFocusedNode`. When focus subsequently escapes to the body (triggering a `focusin` event), `checkFocusIn` attempts to restore focus to the removed button, which fails because it's no longer in the document. Focus then remains on the body instead of being trapped inside the dialog.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify `checkFocusIn` to refresh the trap's tabbable nodes (via `updateTabbableNodes()`) when focus escapes, then verify that `state.mostRecentlyFocusedNode` is still within one of the trap's containers before attempting to restore focus to it. If the node is no longer in a container (e.g., it was removed from the DOM), fall back to `getInitialFocusNode()` which returns the first valid tabbable node in the dialog (the close button).
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: After activating the 'Show all 4 results' button (which removes itself), keyboard focus will remain trapped inside the dialog. Pressing Tab will move focus to the next focusable element in the dialog (e.g., the close button or first list item), allowing the user to continue navigating results.
functional_risks: Calling `updateTabbableNodes()` on every focus escape adds minor overhead, but focus escape is a rare event.

If the trap's containers themselves are dynamically modified, `findContainerIndex` might not reflect the latest state until `updateTabbableNodes()` runs, but this is mitigated by calling it at the start of the escape handler.
verification_requirements: Verify that after clicking 'Show all 4 results', pressing Tab moves focus to the close button (or first focusable element in the dialog).
Ensure that pressing Escape still closes the dialog and returns focus to the opener button.
Test that the focus trap works correctly when focus escapes via other means (e.g., clicking outside the dialog).
